_comment: Alert rules over every host that ships its logs (ADR-039). Heartbeat stays in logging.nix: it must exist before any module has applied its rules.

rules.name: oom-kill
rules.title: OomKill
rules.headline: Out of Memory Kill
rules._comment: Anchored: Loki and Grafana log every rule's query text on the logging VM, and an unanchored rule matches its own query (hrossen, 2026-10-04).
rules.summary: The kernel killed a process for lack of memory.

rules.name: host-silent
rules.title: HostSilent
rules._comment: Every instance that ships (logging:logs, and the logging VM): a deleted one leaves the list in its delete, so it raises nothing (ADR-039 D4). Heartbeat stays in logging.nix.
rules.summary: A host stopped logging 15 minutes ago: it is down, or its log forwarder is (rsyslog on a node, alloy on a VM).

rules.name: ssh-brute-force
rules.title: SshBruteForce
rules.headline: SSH brute force
rules._comment: Anchored: Loki and Grafana log every rule's query text on the logging VM, which is in scope all, so an unanchored rule would match its own query. Per host and per source address. Info: an internet-facing sshd sees scanners all day (hrossen: 75-150 a day per address on the mothership).
rules.match: ^(Failed password for|Invalid user|Connection closed by authenticating user|Disconnected from authenticating user)
rules.summary: More than ten failed SSH logins from one address in five minutes. Key-only SSH makes them harmless: recorded, not raised. A login that then succeeds from that address is SshLoginAfterBruteForce.

rules.name: ssh-login-after-bf
rules.title: SshLoginAfterBruteForce
rules.headline: SSH login after a brute force
rules._comment: Anchored: Loki and Grafana log every rule's query text on the logging VM, which is in scope all, so an unanchored rule would match its own query. A success from an address that failed more than five times in ten minutes, on the same host.
rules.expr: sum by (host, src_ip) (count_over_time(__SELECTOR__ |~ "^(Failed password for|Invalid user)" | regexp "from (?P<src_ip>[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)" [10m])) > 5 and on (host, src_ip) sum by (host, src_ip) (count_over_time(__SELECTOR__ |~ "^Accepted (password|publickey|keyboard-interactive)" | regexp "from (?P<src_ip>[0-9a-fA-F:.]+)" [10m])) > 0
rules.summary: An SSH login succeeded from an address that had just failed many times on the same host. Check who logged in, and acknowledge with the reason (health-manager ack <ci> --type threat --note ...).

rules.name: ssh-password-login
rules.title: SshPasswordLogin
rules.headline: SSH password login
rules._comment: Anchored: Loki and Grafana log every rule's query text on the logging VM, which is in scope all, so an unanchored rule would match its own query. TAPPaaS SSH is key-only: a password that works is a host whose sshd was changed.
rules.summary: An SSH login with a password succeeded. TAPPaaS hosts take keys only, so this host's SSH configuration was changed.

rules.name: sudo-refused
rules.title: SudoRefused
rules.headline: sudo refused
rules._comment: Anchored: Loki and Grafana log every rule's query text on the logging VM, which is in scope all, so an unanchored rule would match its own query. The tappaas user's sudo needs no password: a failure is someone else.
rules.match: ^(pam_unix\(sudo:auth\): authentication failure|\S+ : (user NOT in sudoers|\d+ incorrect password attempts?))
rules.summary: sudo was refused on this host: a wrong password, or a user who may not use it.

rules.name: audit-stopped
rules.title: AuditStopped
rules.headline: Audit logging stopped
rules._comment: Anchored: Loki and Grafana log every rule's query text on the logging VM, which is in scope all, so an unanchored rule would match its own query. Also seen at a planned shutdown; a reboot outside the update window is worth a look anyway. Not the boot's own 'state=initialized audit_enabled=0' (seen on hrossen).
rules.summary: The audit daemon stopped, or auditing was switched off in the kernel: changes on this host are no longer recorded.

rules.name: kernel-module-session
rules.title: KernelModuleFromSession
rules.headline: Kernel module loaded from a session
rules._comment: Audit records on the journal's audit transport (ADR-050 P2; NixOS guests with security monitoring on). Anchored on the record type, so the rule never matches its own query text on the logging VM. Changes to /etc/secrets and SSH keys are recorded (kept 90 days) but raise nothing: updates write them.
rules.summary: A kernel module was loaded or removed from a login session, not by the system at boot. Expected only while someone is debugging hardware; otherwise a sign of tampering.
